paragraphs: Video generators often work with compressed representations rather than full video frames. Many diffusion systems inherit an image encoder from a text-to-image model and reduce temporal information by sampling frames. The paper identifies two problems: frame sampling can produce uneven motion, while introducing a separately trained video encoder can create a representation mismatch that is expensive to overcome.

CV-VAE addresses these problems by training a video variational autoencoder whose compressed representation remains compatible with that of an existing image autoencoder. A regularization loss uses the image autoencoder to guide this compatibility. The authors also introduce an architecture intended to make training more efficient.

This design lets pretrained image or video generators work with representations that compress both space and time. Compatibility matters because it supports reuse of existing generators while changing how video is encoded. The authors report that existing video models can generate four times as many frames with minimal fine-tuning, with extensive experiments supporting the proposed approach.
neurips-2024-cv-vae-a-compatible-video-v.tldr: CV-VAE compresses video across space and time while keeping its representations compatible with pretrained image-based generators.

paragraphs: Federated learning lets devices train a shared model while keeping their data local. Edge devices nevertheless differ in their resources, and their data can come from different domains. These differences make it difficult for one training framework to serve all clients effectively. DapperFL addresses device heterogeneity and differences between local data domains together.

Its Model Fusion Pruning module produces compact models tailored to individual clients. Before pruning, it combines knowledge from the client's own domain and other domains, helping the resulting model handle domain shifts. A Domain Adaptive Regularization module then uses guidance generated by the pruned model to encourage representations that work across domains.

The framework also includes an aggregation procedure for combining local models with different architectures and weights. The authors implement it on a real federated learning platform with heterogeneous clients. Across multidomain benchmark datasets, they report improvements of up to 2.28% over several leading frameworks and model size reductions of 20% to 80%, supporting the usefulness of jointly adapting model size and domain knowledge.
neurips-2024-dapperfl-domain-adaptive-fe.tldr: DapperFL combines domain-aware pruning, regularization, and aggregation to train smaller personalized models across heterogeneous devices.

paragraphs: Controlling a real graphical interface requires reacting to changing screens and unpredictable outcomes. A vision-language model may understand screenshots without having learned how to make effective sequential decisions. The paper shows that training on fixed human demonstrations also leaves important gaps because those examples do not capture all the variability encountered during interaction.

DigiRL fine-tunes a pretrained vision-language model through offline reinforcement learning followed by an offline-to-online stage. The authors build an Android training environment that supports parallel interaction and includes a general-purpose evaluator based on a vision-language model. They also identify design choices that make reinforcement learning effective in this setting.

Using Android-in-the-Wild, the authors report that their 1.5-billion-parameter model improves from 17.7% success with supervised demonstration training to 67.2% with DigiRL. This is a 49.5-percentage-point increase without additional supervision or demonstration data. It also exceeds their filtered behavior cloning implementation at 57.8%. These results support learning from interaction as a way to handle the dynamics of real device control.
neurips-2024-digirl-training-in-the-wild.tldr: DigiRL improves Android device control by training a vision-language model with offline and online reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: A reinforcement learning policy may perform poorly when deployment differs from training. Distributionally robust learning addresses this by optimizing performance in the worst environment within a specified uncertainty set. This paper studies how to learn such a policy when the agent can collect data only by interacting with the training environment.

The authors establish a fundamental obstacle: sample-efficient learning is impossible in general without additional assumptions. The issue is support shift, where deployment may involve outcomes that training interactions cannot reveal. The learner must therefore manage more than the usual exploration problem; some relevant deployment behavior may lie outside what it can observe.

For uncertainty sets defined using total-variation distance, the authors introduce a sufficient condition: the smallest value of the optimal robust value function is zero. They prove that this condition removes the support-shift obstacle in that setting and give an algorithm with a sample-complexity guarantee. The contribution identifies both a general hardness result and a specific assumption under which efficient interactive robust learning becomes possible.
neurips-2024-distributionally-robust-rei.tldr: The paper establishes a barrier to interactive robust reinforcement learning and a sufficient condition that enables sample-efficient learning.

paragraphs: Driving world models predict how a driving scene develops, including its physical dynamics. Their ability to learn this behavior depends on the situations represented in training videos. The paper argues that limited diversity in existing driving datasets restricts the potential of these models, particularly when predictions must respond to driving actions.

DrivingDojo is a dataset designed specifically for training interactive driving world models. Its video clips cover a full set of driving maneuvers, varied interactions among multiple road participants, and broad driving knowledge from open-world situations. These ingredients target the complexity of driving as an interactive process, where future events involve more than the movement of one vehicle.

The authors also introduce an action instruction following benchmark for world models. This makes responsiveness to action instructions an explicit evaluation target alongside future prediction. Their results demonstrate the proposed dataset's advantage for generating futures controlled by actions. The contribution therefore connects richer training examples with an evaluation focused on whether a world model follows the intended driving behavior.
neurips-2024-drivingdojo-dataset-advanci.tldr: DrivingDojo provides diverse driving videos and an action-following benchmark for training interactive driving world models.

paragraphs: Sharpness-Aware Minimization, or SAM, is a gradient-based training method associated with improved generalization in deep neural networks. This paper examines its optimization foundations: what happens to its gradients, objective values, and parameter updates as training proceeds. These are distinct questions, and answering one does not by itself establish all the others.

The analysis establishes several convergence properties within its theoretical framework. These include stationarity of accumulation points, gradients approaching zero, objective values approaching the optimal value, and iterates approaching an optimal solution. Accumulation points describe locations approached by subsequences of updates, whereas convergence of the iterates concerns the entire sequence.

The authors organize their analysis through an inexact gradient descent framework. This shared perspective allows extensions to normalized SAM variants, including F-SAM, VaSSO, and RSAM, as well as the unnormalized USAM variant. Classification experiments with deep learning models support practical aspects of the analysis. The contribution is a framework for studying convergence across related methods, rather than an experimental comparison alone.
neurips-2024-fundamental-convergence-ana.tldr: The paper develops a convergence framework for SAM and extends it to several normalized and unnormalized variants.

paragraphs: Linear stochastic approximation estimates parameters through repeated updates based on observations. This paper studies uncertainty in those estimates when the step size decreases and the iterates are combined using Polyak-Ruppert averaging. Its focus is how reliably the averaged estimate can be described by a multivariate normal distribution.

The authors derive a Berry–Esseen bound, which quantifies the error in that normal approximation. Such a bound provides more information than a statement about behavior only in the limit of infinitely many observations. They also prove finite-sample validity for confidence intervals constructed using a multiplier bootstrap procedure.

The bootstrap operates alongside the estimator as observations arrive. It updates both the main estimate and a collection of randomly perturbed estimates, using their variation to support uncertainty estimation. The authors illustrate the results in temporal difference learning with linear function approximation. Together, the approximation bound and bootstrap guarantee connect an online parameter-estimation procedure to mathematically supported confidence intervals, rather than providing parameter estimates without a measure of uncertainty.
neurips-2024-gaussian-approximation-and-.tldr: The paper proves normal-approximation bounds and finite-sample bootstrap confidence guarantees for averaged linear stochastic approximation.

paragraphs: Large linear programs can be costly to solve. This paper learns a dimensionality-reduction matrix from previous problems so that future problems can be solved in a smaller space. An original problem with n variables is reduced to k dimensions, and the learned matrix maps the smaller solution back into the original space.

The theoretical question is how much training data is sufficient to obtain reliable solution quality on future instances. The authors analyze pseudo-dimension, a measure of the complexity of the performance functions involved. They establish an upper bound of order nk squared, up to logarithmic factors, and a lower bound of order nk. This leaves a gap of roughly a factor of k, again allowing logarithmic factors.

For learning the projection, the paper explores PCA-based and gradient-based methods. PCA is relatively efficient, while gradient-based learning sometimes gives better solutions. Experiments show better solution quality than existing random projections while greatly reducing solving time. The results connect a practical compression strategy with theory about learning projections that generalize.
neurips-2024-generalization-bound-and-le.tldr: Learning projection matrices from past linear programs improves compressed solution quality, with generalization bounds supporting the approach.

paragraphs: A learnware pairs a trained model with a specification describing what it can do. A collection of these packages is meant to help users reuse existing models instead of training new ones. The difficulty addressed here is that available models may use feature spaces different from those of the user's task, leaving few or no direct matches.

The paper identifies model outputs as useful information that earlier approaches have not fully exploited. It extends learnware specifications with pseudo-labels, meaning labels supplied by models. This information also enriches the shared embedding space in which specifications are represented and developed, giving the system additional evidence about model capabilities.

Label information further improves model identification through comparisons of conditional distributions. This adds a label-dependent perspective to matching models across different feature spaces. Experiments show that the system can handle user tasks using models from diverse feature spaces even when no model was explicitly tailored to the task. The result supports broader reuse through better descriptions and selection of existing models.
neurips-2024-handling-learnwares-from-he.tldr: Using model-generated labels helps a learnware system identify and reuse models whose feature spaces differ from the user's task.

paragraphs: Test-time prompt tuning adapts a vision model's prompts using unlabeled samples encountered during inference. This offers adaptation without task-specific annotations, but continued updates can degrade performance. The paper highlights that the problem becomes more severe when incoming samples repeatedly shift between domains.

HisTPT addresses this by retaining useful knowledge from previously processed samples. It introduces three stores: a local knowledge bank, a hard-sample knowledge bank, and a global knowledge bank. Each uses a different mechanism to support memory and prompt optimization. The aim is to make ongoing adaptation benefit from what has already been learned.

An adaptive retrieval mechanism chooses stored knowledge to regularize the prediction for each new sample. This connects historical information to current decisions instead of relying on continued prompt updates alone. Experiments report consistently stronger prompt tuning across image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection, including streams with continuously changing domains. The findings support memory and selective retrieval as useful components of sustained adaptation without labeled test data.
neurips-2024-historical-test-time-prompt.tldr: HisTPT uses historical knowledge banks and adaptive retrieval to stabilize prompt tuning as unlabeled test data changes.

paragraphs: This paper studies allocating indivisible goods over time when the allocator does not know how much each player values an arriving item. There are finitely many types of goods, and players' values follow distributions with unknown means. The objective is to maximize total welfare while preserving fairness in expectation.

The authors translate the problem into a stochastic bandit setting, with an arm for each player and type of good. At each step, a probability distribution over arms determines allocation. They consider two fairness requirements: envy-freeness in expectation and proportionality in expectation. These requirements concern expected allocations and values, rather than guaranteeing fairness for every individual realized item.

Their explore-then-commit algorithm first gathers information and then uses what it has learned for subsequent allocations. It achieves regret of order T to the two-thirds power, up to logarithmic factors, while maintaining either fairness constraint. The proof exploits particular properties of fair-division constraints, showing how meaningful learning guarantees remain possible despite restrictions on the available allocation decisions.
neurips-2024-honor-among-bandits-no-regr.tldr: An explore-then-commit algorithm learns valuable allocations while maintaining envy-freeness or proportionality in expectation.

paragraphs: Distilled diffusion models can generate images in only a few sampling steps, but fast generation does not automatically preserve every capability of the original model. This paper focuses on inversion: encoding a real image into the model's latent space. Accurate inversion matters because many precise editing methods depend on representing the starting image faithfully.

The authors introduce invertible Consistency Distillation, or iCD, to support both image synthesis and image encoding. Their framework performs these operations in three to four inference steps. It extends consistency distillation so that speed is paired with the ability to move a real image into a representation suitable for manipulation.

The paper also examines classifier-free guidance, whose high settings make inversion harder. The authors find that dynamic guidance substantially reduces reconstruction errors without a noticeable decline in generation performance. Combining iCD with this guidance strategy enables zero-shot editing directed by text. The reported results suggest that the combination can compete with more computationally expensive leading editing methods.
neurips-2024-invertible-consistency-dist.tldr: iCD combines fast image generation and inversion with dynamic guidance to enable efficient text-guided editing.

paragraphs: Dimensionality reduction places complex data into a smaller representation. Parametric methods learn a mapping that can also be applied to unseen data, making them attractive for reuse. This paper challenges the assumption that this convenience comes with performance equivalent to non-parametric approaches, particularly when preserving fine local relationships.

The authors find that parametric methods preserve broad global structure while losing substantial local detail. Their evidence points to difficulty pushing negative samples apart, with the choice of loss function also contributing. This identifies separation between samples as an important part of the problem, alongside the ability to represent the overall arrangement of the data.

Their proposed method, ParamRepulsor, combines hard negative mining with a loss that imposes strong repulsion. Hard negative mining directs attention toward negative samples that are difficult to separate. The method achieves leading local-structure preservation among parametric approaches without sacrificing global structural fidelity. The findings connect a specific weakness in learned mappings to a training strategy designed to address it.
neurips-2024-navigating-the-effect-of-pa.tldr: ParamRepulsor improves local detail in parametric dimensionality reduction through hard negative mining and stronger repulsion.

paragraphs: Adaptive gradient methods are widely used in deep learning, but their theory often assumes gradient estimates are unbiased. Some learning systems use Monte Carlo procedures that do not satisfy that assumption. This paper studies adaptive stochastic optimization when gradient estimates have bias, including bias that changes over time.

The analysis concerns smooth, non-convex objectives and gives guarantees for finite amounts of computation. It emphasizes controlling estimation bias and establishes convergence to critical points for Adagrad, RMSProp, and AMSGRAD with biased gradients. The reported rates are similar to existing results for unbiased gradients. Convergence to a critical point concerns vanishing gradients; it does not by itself identify a global optimum.

The authors also present experiments with variational autoencoders and applications to several learning frameworks. These illustrate the theoretical results and show that suitable hyperparameter tuning can reduce the influence of bias. The contribution connects adaptive optimization theory to settings where unbiased estimation is unavailable, while making bias control an explicit part of the convergence analysis.
neurips-2024-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.tldr: The paper analyzes adaptive optimization with biased gradients and shows how controlling bias supports convergence for smooth non-convex objectives.

paragraphs: Time series often contain several repeating patterns at once. Weather and traffic, for example, can vary over daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly cycles. The paper argues that directly modeling a one-dimensional sequence makes these overlapping periodic patterns difficult to capture, particularly when their relationships are complex.

Peri-midFormer organizes the sequence into a periodic pyramid. The original series sits at the top, and lower levels contain components with progressively shorter periods. This representation explicitly describes how periodic components contain and overlap one another, giving the model a structured way to work with multiple timescales.

The model then applies self-attention between components according to inclusion, overlap, and adjacency relationships. Attention therefore operates on the periodic organization as part of learning temporal variation. The authors report strong performance across short-term forecasting, long-term forecasting, missing-value imputation, classification, and anomaly detection. These results suggest that the same representation can support several kinds of time-series analysis, rather than serving only one prediction horizon or task.
neurips-2024-peri-midformer-periodic-pyr.tldr: Peri-midFormer organizes repeating patterns into a hierarchy and uses attention to model relationships across timescales.

paragraphs: A world model can become good at predicting details that do not help an agent choose actions. This is a particular vulnerability when model-based reinforcement learning trains the model to reconstruct observations. Intricate but predictable background content can consume capacity that would otherwise describe dynamics relevant to the policy.

The authors introduce an environment designed to expose this problem, with background distractions that are predictable yet useless for planning. They show that the issue continues to affect leading methods, including DreamerV3 and DreamerPro. This separates success at modeling visible content from success at learning information useful for control.

Their proposed method combines a pretrained segmentation model, a task-aware reconstruction loss, and adversarial learning to direct world-model capacity toward useful information. The components work together to make prediction more sensitive to the needs of policy learning. The method outperforms several approaches intended to suppress distractors. The results support treating the relevance of predicted content as a central design concern for robust model-based reinforcement learning.
neurips-2024-policy-shaped-prediction-av.tldr: Policy-shaped prediction helps world models focus on information useful for control when predictable backgrounds create distractions.

paragraphs: Spiking transformers combine spiking neural networks with transformer architectures, aiming for strong performance with low energy use. Their accuracy has nevertheless lagged behind conventional neural networks. QKFormer addresses this gap through changes to attention, the organization of representations, and the transmission of spiking information.

Its Q-K attention module uses binary vectors to model attention across tokens or channels. The authors describe this module as having linear complexity and high energy efficiency, supporting larger models. A hierarchical structure varies token counts across blocks to produce representations at multiple scales. A specialized patch embedding component, SPEDS, further improves information transmission and integration.

The authors report superior performance over existing leading spiking networks on several mainstream datasets. On ImageNet-1k, QKFormer reaches 85.65% top-1 accuracy with 64.96 million parameters, compared with Spikformer's 74.81% at 66.34 million parameters. The 10.84-percentage-point improvement occurs at comparable model size. The authors identify this, to their knowledge, as the first directly trained spiking network to exceed 85% accuracy on that benchmark.
neurips-2024-qkformer-hierarchical-spiki.tldr: QKFormer combines binary Q-K attention and hierarchical spiking representations to improve accuracy at comparable model size.

paragraphs: In a Stackelberg game, a leader commits to a strategy and a follower responds to it. Real decisions also depend on shared circumstances such as weather or network congestion. This paper incorporates that side information by allowing both players to observe a context before choosing their behavior.

The authors study repeated play with a sequence of followers and contexts that can change each round. The leader chooses a context-dependent strategy, and each follower best-responds to both that strategy and the observed context. They show that good regret performance is impossible when both sequences can be chosen adversarially, unlike the corresponding setting without context.

The paper then identifies two relaxations that allow no-regret learning. In one, followers are drawn stochastically while contexts remain adversarial. In the other, contexts are stochastic while followers are chosen adversarially. These results establish that which part of the environment has statistical regularity matters: either source of randomness can restore learnability in the respective setting despite adversarial variation in the other.
neurips-2024-regret-minimization-in-stac.tldr: Context makes fully adversarial Stackelberg learning impossible, but no-regret learning becomes possible when followers or contexts are stochastic.

paragraphs: Safety behavior in a language model can be weakened through harmful fine-tuning. This creates a problem even when a model initially refuses harmful requests, particularly if an attacker can modify its weights. Representation Noising, or RepNoise, aims to make harmful capabilities harder to recover through subsequent training.

The defense removes information from harmful internal representations. The authors provide empirical evidence that its effectiveness depends on depth: removing such information throughout the model's layers matters. They also report that the method preserves general capabilities and the ability to fine-tune on harmless tasks, making continued legitimate adaptation part of the evaluation.

The reported generalization has a specific condition. RepNoise can extend to harmful subsets not encountered during defense training when they come from the same distribution as the attack set. The authors also identify settings where the defense remains ineffective. The findings therefore support representation-level resistance to harmful fine-tuning while retaining an explicit boundary on generalization and acknowledging that the defense does not succeed everywhere.
neurips-2024-representation-noising-a-de.tldr: RepNoise removes harmful information across model layers to resist harmful fine-tuning while preserving useful capabilities in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Language-model unlearning aims to remove knowledge associated with specified documents while preserving other capabilities. The setting here assumes access to a small collection of documents representing knowledge to retain. Common approaches raise prediction loss on forget documents while lowering it on retain documents, but this can damage output quality and cause broader forgetting.

Unlearning from Logit Difference, or ULD, trains an assistant model with reversed objectives. The assistant learns the forget documents and forgets the retain knowledge. The unlearned model is then derived by subtracting the assistant's logits, or prediction scores, from those of the target model. This makes the assistant's opposite training goals central to the unlearning mechanism.

Experiments show effective forgetting with preservation of overall capabilities and a greater than threefold reduction in training time. On ToFU, the authors report no loss of model utility, while baseline methods may lose 17% on average at comparable forgetting quality. These results support the framework's efficiency and preservation benefits in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2024-reversing-the-forget-retain.tldr: ULD trains an assistant with reversed forgetting objectives and subtracts its prediction scores to achieve efficient language-model unlearning.

paragraphs: A policy can earn a large return while consuming substantial resources. ROIDICE studies efficiency by defining return on investment as total return divided by accumulated cost. The goal is to learn a policy that maximizes this ratio using a fixed dataset in a Markov decision process with an explicit cost function.

This objective is difficult because both the numerator and denominator describe long-term outcomes of decisions. The authors formulate the problem as linear fractional programming, giving the ratio objective a mathematical optimization structure. They then combine this formulation with stationary distribution correction, known as DICE, to build a practical offline learning algorithm.

The resulting algorithm targets the relationship between reward and expenditure directly. The authors report that ROIDICE produces policies with a better trade-off between return and accumulated cost than policies trained with existing frameworks. The contribution is therefore both an objective and a method: it makes efficiency the quantity being optimized and provides a way to pursue it from previously collected data.
neurips-2024-roidice-offline-return-on-i.tldr: ROIDICE learns policies from fixed data by directly maximizing the ratio of long-term return to accumulated cost.

paragraphs: Image quantization represents images using discrete tokens selected from a codebook. Expanding that codebook is useful only if the model actually uses the additional entries. The paper identifies limited size and low utilization as persistent problems in VQGAN variants, with VQGAN-FC typically using less than 12% of its codebook on ImageNet.

VQGAN-LC changes how the codebook is built and aligned. It starts with 100,000 features extracted by a pretrained vision encoder. Instead of optimizing each entry independently, it trains a projector that aligns the whole codebook with the feature distribution of the VQGAN-LC encoder. The reported utilization exceeds 99%.

The authors evaluate the representation in image reconstruction, image classification, autoregressive generation with GPT, and generation using diffusion and flow models. They report better performance than counterpart methods across these tasks. This breadth matters because a codebook is a shared representation component: improvements can support both recovering images from tokens and learning models that use those tokens for other purposes.
neurips-2024-scaling-the-codebook-size-o.tldr: VQGAN-LC aligns a pretrained-feature codebook through a learned projector, enabling 100,000 entries with over 99% utilization.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning a vision-language model on one distribution should ideally preserve performance when inputs change. Accuracy alone does not establish reliability, however: confidence should also reflect how often predictions are correct. This paper addresses out-of-distribution accuracy and confidence calibration together during adaptation.

The authors derive a shared upper bound for out-of-distribution classification and calibration errors. It involves two quantities from the training distribution: calibration error and the smallest singular value of the input covariance matrix. This connects behavior under distribution shift to both confidence quality and the structure of in-distribution inputs.

The proposed method uses a constrained multimodal contrastive loss that encourages a larger smallest singular value. Self-distillation from a moving-averaged model provides additional guidance toward calibrated predictions. Experiments on ImageNet distribution-shift benchmarks support the theoretical statements and the practical method. The contribution is a linked treatment of two reliability concerns, using one analytical perspective to motivate training changes that improve both reported accuracy and calibration.
neurips-2024-towards-calibrated-robust-f.tldr: The paper connects shifted-distribution accuracy and calibration through a shared bound and uses it to guide robust fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Diffusion models that accept both visual and language inputs can transfer concepts into generated images. This flexibility also creates misuse concerns, including unauthorized copying of artistic styles. The paper addresses control over unsafe concepts and argues that existing interventions often struggle with effectiveness or scalability.

Causal representation editing, or CRE, extends representation-editing ideas from language models to diffusion generation. It intervenes at diffusion timesteps identified as causally connected to unsafe concepts. The approach targets when those concepts influence generation, aiming to remove harmful content while maintaining the quality of acceptable content.

The authors report advantages in effectiveness, precision, and scalability over existing methods. They also show that CRE can handle cases where unsafe concepts appear through incomplete or blurred representations. These findings matter because concept control must operate on the representations available during generation, which may be imperfect. The contribution is a targeted intervention framework that connects causal information about the generation process to more selective editing of its output.
neurips-2024-towards-safe-concept-transf.tldr: CRE targets diffusion timesteps causally linked to unsafe concepts to remove harmful content while preserving acceptable image quality.

paragraphs: Human demonstrations can contain several valid ways to act, making behavior learning a problem of representing diverse possibilities. Diffusion policies handle this complexity well, but repeated sampling steps slow inference and their likelihoods are intractable. These properties create difficulties for applications such as real-time robot control.

Variational Diffusion Distillation, or VDD, transfers a pretrained diffusion policy into a mixture of experts. Such mixtures can represent complex distributions while addressing the diffusion model's inference and likelihood drawbacks, but training them is difficult. VDD uses variational inference and an upper bound on its objective that separates into parts, allowing each expert to be trained independently.

This decomposition provides a more robust optimization scheme for the mixture. Across nine complex behavior-learning tasks, the authors report accurate transfer of the diffusion model's distributions, better results than existing leading distillation methods, and improvements over conventional mixture-of-experts training. The findings support using a trained diffusion model to teach a policy representation better suited to efficient inference.
neurips-2024-variational-distillation-of.tldr: VDD distills diffusion policies into mixtures of experts using a decomposable variational objective that trains experts separately.
